Both supplied units are base-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (base lines 784-1017 and 1018-1323). No patch hunks or head text were provided, so the actual PR delta is not visible. This is a coverage limit, not evidence the change is safe. The excerpts are documentation only and execute nothing. They describe pre-existing behavior that already maps to the threat model: App Attest coexistence and protocol 3 (TB-011, T-052..T-058), the SSD prefix cache (T-041, TB-007), the request profiler (T-051), Stripe/Connect withdrawals (TB-008, T-030), stats/geography, and release-candidate notes. Two details the next pass should check against the threat model:
- The changelog (lines 1128, 998) describes the SSD disk budget as half of available disk space without a fixed ceiling. This matches T-041. Line 1128 ("100 GiB ceiling") is older history that later entries supersede.
- The T-041 30-minute TTL is not mentioned in these lines, so a TTL change in another file would need an independent sign-off.
No security-relevant behavior change can be attributed to these units. Later passes should examine the code files in the PR, particularly the coordinator App Attest, profiler and payout paths and the provider SSD cache. They should confirm that any changelog claim added by the PR matches the code and the TB-011 and T-041 assumptions.
